description: Declarative distribution manifest for the Rust product (issue 0036). Generated documents go to releaseOutputDir, which is not committed, never into this file or docs/third-party/. Nothing here publishes, tags, uploads or reserves anything.

sourceDateEpoch.notes: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH when set and valid, otherwise the HEAD commit time. The wall clock is never read, because a document that differs every run cannot be diffed, and diffing is the only mechanism that has actually held for docs/RUST-DEPENDENCIES.md and NOTICE.

artifacts.description: The command-line application, with release inventory coverage separate from the staged frontend bundle.
artifacts.binaryLayout: cargo's own layout under the active target directory: <target-dir>/release/<binaryName> for a host build and <target-dir>/<triple>/release/<binaryName> for a cross build. The target directory is CARGO_TARGET_DIR when set, otherwise target/. It is derived rather than declared because a declared path drifts from cargo's layout silently, and CI and parallel worktrees both move the target directory.
artifacts.targetEvidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml: the cross-build job builds x86_64/aarch64 linux-gnu for real, and the macos-15 job installs both darwin triples. These are the targets a binary is actually produced for, not an aspiration.

artifacts.description: The macOS bundle of the actively developed frontend. This locally runnable interface redistributes a Flutter engine, an AOT-compiled Dart runtime, plugin frameworks and a Material icon font, none of which cargo metadata can see. Declared so the obligation is visible, not to claim completed release coverage.

implemented: rust: the bridge crate's own resolved graph, from its OWN workspace (it is excluded from the root one, so root-workspace metadata does not describe it)
rust: the standard library, from the pinned toolchain record
dart: every package resolved in pubspec.lock, classified direct/transitive and sdk/hosted/path
requiresBuiltBundle: the Flutter engine framework and its version
plugin and platform frameworks actually embedded, with their digests
fonts and other flutter_assets entries shipped in the bundle
coverage.notes: Running without --bundle emits a document explicitly marked incomplete and exits non-zero when --release-grade is asked for. That is a staged gap with a named owner (issue 0024 / platform0024), not a refusal to cover the artifact kind.

artifacts.description: The browser editor (issue 0088, ADR 0012): the Flutter web application with CanvasKit served from the bundle, and the Rust core compiled to wasm32-wasip1 (domowik_bridge.wasm). Built by frontend/scripts/build-web.sh into frontend/build/web. Its 3D renderer module is the separate domowik-gui-web-renderer artifact in the same bundle.

implemented: rust: the bridge crate's resolved graph for wasm32-wasip1, from its own workspace
rust: the standard library, from the pinned toolchain record
dart: every package resolved in pubspec.lock, classified direct/transitive and sdk/hosted/path
requiresBuiltBundle: the CanvasKit engine files and the compiled main.dart.js
fonts and other assets entries shipped in the bundle
coverage.notes: Staged like the macOS bundle: the Rust and Dart halves are audited here; the web engine files are listed from a built bundle and are not licence-resolved by the scan.

artifacts.description: The browser editor's 3D renderer module (issue 0088, ADR 0012): the shared wgpu renderer on WebGPU for wasm32-unknown-unknown, with its wasm-bindgen JavaScript glue (domowik_renderer.js, domowik_renderer_bg.wasm), shipped in the same bundle as domowik-gui-web.

implemented: rust: the web renderer crate's resolved graph for wasm32-unknown-unknown, including wgpu's WebGPU backend and wasm-bindgen, from the frontend workspace
rust: the standard library, from the pinned toolchain record
requiresBuiltBundle: the generated wasm-bindgen glue, which is wasm-bindgen output under its MIT/Apache-2.0 terms
coverage.notes: Shares the domowik-gui-web bundle; listed separately because it is a second Rust graph on a second target.

bundledAssetPolicy.notes: Every file compiled into an artifact by include_bytes!/include_str! must have a row in the assets record. scripts/release-validate.py scans for them and fails closed on an undeclared one. Before this scan nothing checked: the assets record is hand-maintained, so an undeclared embed changed no generated file and failed no stage.
